verdicts.reason: A breaks the reading order: the product can is jammed against the left and top edges, the CTA sits stranded in the middle, and the logo is pushed to the far right after the CTA. B reads logo → product → headline → CTA from left to right, but the product is tiny, the subline is small and there is a large dead gap between the copy and the CTA.

A has a larger, stronger headline, but the CTA almost touches the right edge, the logo is shrunk, and the gap from logo to product is uneven. B has the same order with more even margins around the CTA, but its headline and subline are smaller and there is still dead space between the copy and the button. Both use a tiny product can.

A has a steady left-to-right flow with acceptable margins, though the product is tiny and there is a gap before the CTA. B shrinks the logo, leaves a big empty hole between the logo and the product (which drifts to the centre), and crowds the CTA against the right edge, so its weight is lopsided.
